items.title: ConocoPhillips CFO to Ascend to Top Role; Fast-Food Burger Battle; Plus, New Layoff Data
items.summary: ConocoPhillips CFO Andy O’Brien is the latest finance chief to step into the top job, with current CEO Ryan Lance retiring next month after 14 years.  The leadership change comes as U.S. oil giant  ConocoPhillips  reported its best quarterly results in four years, with profits of $3.9 billion, boosted by higher oil and fuel prices amid the Iran war, our WSJ colleague Benoît Morenne reports.  CFO background and cred: O’Brien joined the company in 1997 and has held several finance, planning and strategy roles throughout his time.

items.title: ConocoPhillips (COP) Names Andy O'Brien CEO To Succeed Ryan Lance In 2026
items.summary: ConocoPhillips (NYSE:COP) announced that Andy O'Brien will succeed Ryan Lance as president and CEO effective September 1, 2026. The planned succession marks a scheduled leadership transition at the top of the oil and gas company. Ryan Lance is expected to remain in his current role until the handover to support an orderly change in leadership.
